title: 欧洲接连发生炸弹威胁事件，意大利数百所学校紧急疏散
description: JONATHAN WOLFE, LEO SANDS, ELISABETTA POVOLEDO, ALI WATKINS2026年11月12日周三，意大利都灵一所学校外，学生们因炸弹威胁被疏散。 Marco Alpozzi/LaPresse, via Associated Press Hundreds of schools in Italy and elsewhere in Europe were evacuated on Wednesday after receiving emailed bomb threats that were determined to be hoaxes, officials said, adding to disruptions after flights and news outlets across the continent were targeted with similar threats last week. 官员表示，意大利及欧洲其他地区数百所学校周三收到含有炸弹威胁的电子邮件后实施疏散，这些威胁后被认定为虚假信息。此前一周，欧洲大陆多架航班和多家新闻机构也遭遇类似威胁，进一步加剧了混乱。 The latest messages, which were also sent to schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland, appeared to be part of a coordinated campaign to sow confusion across Europe, officials said, even as they indicated that they did not know who was behind them. 官员表示，最新一批信息还发送给了苏格兰和北爱尔兰的学校，似乎是一场意图在欧洲各地制造混乱的协同行动的一部分，尽管他们同时表示尚不清楚幕后主使是谁。 Italy’s education minister, Giuseppe Valditara, said that at least 300 schools had received the anonymous threats. He said that Italy’s intelligence agencies were investigating and suggested a link to other recent disruptions in Europe, including apparent cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems and blood banks. 意大利教育部长朱塞佩·瓦尔迪塔拉表示，至少300所学校收到了匿名威胁。他称意大利情报机构正在调查，并暗示此事与欧洲近期其他干扰事件存在关联，包括针对超市制冷系统和血库的疑似网络攻击。 “It’s not the first time,” Mr. Valditara told “l’Aria che Tira,” a morning talk show on the La7 channel in Italy. “We obviously need to be vigilant, but we must also be aware that in a context where hybrid warfare is increasingly being used as a tool to destabilize nations and economies, we need to prepare ourselves.” 瓦尔迪塔拉对意大利La7频道早间脱口秀节目《风向》(L’Aria che Tira)表示：“这不是第一次了。我们显然需要保持警惕，但也必须意识到，在混合战争日益被用作破坏国家和经济稳定工具的背景之下，我们需要做好准备。” Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni of Italy called a meeting for Wednesday afternoon with ministers and cybersecurity officials but said that “at this time, the investigations conducted have not revealed any evidence to suggest that a concrete danger exists.” 意大利总理焦尔吉娅·梅洛尼周三下午召集部长和网络安全官员开会，但她表示“目前进行的调查未发现任何证据表明存在具体危险”。 “Rather,” she added in a statement on social media, “they appear to be part of a strategy aimed at causing alarm and concern.” “倒像是一种制造恐慌和忧虑的策略的一部分，”她在社交媒体声明中补充道。 The police in Scotland said that “threatening messages were sent to a number of schools” on Wednesday morning. “These messages were immediately assessed and are being treated as hoaxes,” the police said in a statement, adding that they were not advising schools to evacuate. 苏格兰警方表示，周三上午“威胁信息被发送给了多所学校”。“这些信息经即时评估后被认定为虚假威胁，”警方在声明中说，并表示不建议学校疏散。 Similar emails sent to schools across Northern Ireland were “being treated as a hoax,” the country’s Education Authority said in a statement, adding, “We strongly condemn these malicious emails and the distress and disruption caused to school communities.” 北爱尔兰教育局在声明中表示，发送给多所学校的类似电子邮件“正被作为虚假威胁处理”，并称“我们强烈谴责这些恶意邮件及其给学校社区造成的痛苦和混乱”。 Officials have emphasized that the extent of the threats remains limited. The number of flights affected last week, for example, was a fraction of the tens of thousands that operate daily in Europe. But anxiety is running high on the continent, where hybrid warfare attacks and intimidation tactics have shaken air travel and other industries in recent months as Russia’s war against Ukraine spills over its borders. 官员强调，威胁的范围仍然有限。例如，上周受影响的航班数量仅是欧洲每日数万架次中的一小部分。但整个欧洲大陆的焦虑情绪持续高涨。近几个月来，混合战争攻击和恐吓手段已动摇航空旅行及其他行业，与此同时俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争外溢至其边境之外。 What happened last week? 上周发生了什么？ 周五，布拉格瓦茨拉夫·哈维尔机场的航班受到了干扰。 Bomb threats targeted several European airlines, disrupting dozens of flights and forcing emergency landings, some accompanied by military jets. No explosives were found on any of the flights, according to officials. 炸弹威胁针对多家欧洲航空公司，扰乱了数十架次航班并迫使紧急降落，部分航班有战机伴飞。官员称，所有航班上均未发现爆炸物。 On Friday, Czech police said that Prague’s main airport had received threats of explosives placed aboard arriving and departing flights. The Hungarian defense minister, Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, said that Hungarian fighter jets had temporarily escorted one of the flights. 周五，捷克警方表示布拉格主要机场收到威胁，称进出港航班上被放置了爆炸物。匈牙利国防部长罗穆卢斯·鲁辛-森迪表示，匈牙利战机曾临时为一架航班护航。 Officials at Copenhagen’s airport also said that Danish police had responded to threats to flights, without giving details. 哥本哈根机场官员也表示，丹麦警方已对航班所受威胁作出响应，但未提供细节。 A day earlier, officials said that targeted flights included an Aer Lingus plane flying to Rome from Dublin that was diverted to an air base in France; four planes heading to Prague; two LOT Polish Airlines flights, bound for Paris and Brussels; and two Aegean Airlines flights, from Thessaloniki to Milan and from Athens to Vienna. A series of similar threats on Nov. 3 disrupted flights in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy. 一天前，官员称受影响的航班包括一架从都柏林飞往罗马的爱尔兰航空飞机，该航班备降法国一处空军基地；四架飞往布拉格的飞机；两个波兰航空航班，分别飞往巴黎和布鲁塞尔；以及两个爱琴海航空航班，分别从塞萨洛尼基飞往米兰、从雅典飞往维也纳。11月3日的一系列类似威胁扰乱了波兰、西班牙、保加利亚和意大利的航班。 Nerves were further rattled on Friday after the offices of several news media outlets in Ireland and other European countries were evacuated following bomb threats that turned out to be hoaxes. Nova, a Bulgarian news media organization, reported that it had received a bomb threat by email that also claimed responsibility for the threats against planes. 周五，爱尔兰及其他欧洲国家多家新闻媒体机构的办公室在收到炸弹威胁后实施疏散，这些威胁后被证明是虚假的，进一步加剧了紧张情绪。保加利亚新闻机构Nova报道称其收到一封电子邮件炸弹威胁，该邮件还声称对针对飞机的威胁负责。 What are officials saying? 官员们怎么说？ On Friday, after the threats to media companies, the Irish government said in a statement: “It seems likely that this is a coordinated campaign of disruption.” 周五，在媒体公司受到威胁后，爱尔兰政府在声明中表示：“这似乎很可能是一场协同的扰乱行动。” Heidi Alexander, Britain’s transport secretary, told British news media last Thursday that the government was taking the “malicious hoax threats” seriously, but that they were not believed to be credible. 英国交通大臣海蒂·亚历山大上周四对英国新闻媒体表示，政府正在认真对待这些“恶意虚假威胁”，但认为它们并不可信。 Officials at Aeroporti di Roma, which manages Rome’s two commercial airports, said that one threat arrived Thursday morning in an email written in Italian with the subject line “threat notification.” A spokesman for the airport operator said that the email had been sent from “fighters of the male state” who said they wanted to “turn the skies red” with explosions. 管理罗马两座民用机场的罗马机场公司官员表示，其中一条威胁于周四上午通过一封意大利语电子邮件送达，主题为“威胁通知”。该机场运营方发言人称，邮件发件人是“男性国家的战士”，声称他们想用爆炸“把天空变成一片红色”。 Police Scotland noted that the messages on Wednesday were “sent widely to distribution lists across the U.K. and Northern Ireland and our assessment remains that they do not represent a credible threat.” The agency’s Cyber and Fraud Unit was investigating, it said. 苏格兰警察局指出，周三的信息“被广泛发送至英国和北爱尔兰的邮件列表，我们的评估仍然是它们不构成可信威胁”。该机构表示，其网络与欺诈部门正在调查。 What else has Europe on edge? 欧洲还有哪些事件令人不安？ 周五，在遭遇炸弹威胁后，警方在哥本哈根机场巡逻。 A number of European countries have been affected by suspected cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems, including France in October and Ireland, Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg this month. 多个欧洲国家受到针对超市制冷系统的疑似网络攻击影响，包括10月的法国以及本月爱尔兰、瑞典、比利时和卢森堡。 On Monday, French officials accused Iran of orchestrating the October attack and issued international arrest warrants for three Iranians “affiliated with the Electronic and Cyber ​​Center of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps.” 周一，法国官员指责伊朗策划了10月的攻击，并对三名“隶属于伊斯兰革命卫队电子与网络中心”的伊朗人发出国际逮捕令。 And on Nov. 4 France said that a cyberattack had targeted blood banks by raising the temperatures in storage refrigerators. 11月4日，法国表示血库遭到网络攻击，手段是提升储存冰箱的温度。 It is not clear whether the cyberattacks are linked to the bomb threats. 目前尚不清楚这些网络攻击是否与炸弹威胁有关联。 What is the goal? 目的是什么？ Neither the identities of those making the threats nor their motives are clear. But some officials and experts have sought to find a logic behind the targets. For example, Ireland — where media companies and the national air carrier, Aer Lingus, received threats — is hosting summits of European and global leaders this week. 威胁实施者的身份和动机均不明确。但一些官员和专家试图在目标中寻找逻辑。例如，爱尔兰——媒体公司和国有航空公司爱尔兰航空均在其境内收到威胁——本周正在主办欧洲和全球领导人峰会。 Peter Neumann, a professor of security studies at King’s College London, said he saw hallmarks of a hybrid attack: The targets were diffuse, and the goal seemed to be disruption. 伦敦国王学院安全研究教授彼得·诺伊曼表示，他看到了混合攻击的特征：目标分散，目的似乎是制造扰乱。 “The aim of a hybrid campaign is to create chaos, uncertainty and a sense of threat,” he said. “混合行动的目的是制造混乱、不确定性和威胁感，”他说。 (Hybrid warfare involves tactics, including sabotage and disinformation, that are used covertly to destabilize countries and erode trust in institutions without provoking a major military response.) （混合战涉及破坏和虚假信息等战术，被秘密用于破坏国家稳定、侵蚀对机构的信任，同时不引发大规模军事回应。） But analysts agreed that it can be extremely difficult to attribute these kind of threats to any one actor or group with confidence. The Irish government’s statement said it was unclear whether the threats were from “individuals or a centralized or coordinated effort.” 但分析人士一致认为，要将此类威胁明确归因于任何单一行为者或团体极为困难。爱尔兰政府的声明称，尚不清楚威胁来自“个人还是统一协调的行动”。 “Bomb threats are incredibly cheap, and they are low-risk in the sense that they’re pretty easy to obscure,” said Rhys Jones, a security analyst at Osprey, an aviation risk consultancy, meaning a variety of people are capable of performing them, including teenagers or pranksters. “炸弹威胁成本极低，而且风险很低，因为它们很容易隐匿，”航空风险咨询公司Osprey的安全分析师里斯·琼斯说，这意味着各类人群都有能力实施，包括青少年或恶作剧者。 Why are the hoaxes so disruptive? 虚假威胁为何如此具有扰乱性？ Marco Chan, a lecturer in aviation operations at Kingston University in London, said that even if a bomb threat is assessed as a probable hoax, it is difficult for the authorities to determine that for certain without carrying out a thorough search. 伦敦金斯顿大学航空运营讲师马可·陈表示，即使炸弹威胁被评估为很可能是虚假的，当局若不进行彻底搜查，也难以确定。 As a result, he said, if a threat is received while a flight is in the air, the authorities have little choice but to ground the aircraft for emergency inspections. 他说，因此，如果航班在空中时收到威胁，当局别无选择，只能让飞机降落进行紧急检查。 “If there is a shred of concern as to whether there is a bomb threat, they should always treat it as genuine,” Mr. Chan said. “只要对是否存在炸弹威胁有一丝担忧，他们就应始终将其当作真实威胁来对待，”他说。 Jonathan Wolfe 是《纽约时报》驻伦敦记者，报道突发新闻。 Leo Sands 是《纽约时报》突发新闻中心记者，常驻伦敦。 Elisabetta Povoledo 是《纽约时报》记者，常驻罗马，报道意大利新闻、梵蒂冈及该区域文化新闻。她从事新闻业已有35年。 Ali Watkins 为时报报道国际新闻，常驻贝尔法斯特。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

title: 特朗普应对失败的“经典”方式：制造混乱
description: KATIE ROGERS2026年11月11日 Coping with loss looks different for everyone, and President Trump has processed the country’s nearly wholesale rejection of the Republican Party in the midterm elections in his own way. 每个人应对失败的方式都不一样，而特朗普总统正以他自己的方式来消化这个国家在中期选举中对共和党近乎全面的否定。 The last week has seen the president renew false claims about rigged elections, float a mixed martial arts executive as his new press secretary, muse about the beams in the White House ballroom, oust his chief of staff and call unannounced into C-SPAN. 过去一周里，总统重新抛出了关于选举被操纵的虚假指控，提议让一名综合格斗赛事高管担任他的新任新闻秘书，念叨着白宫宴会厅的横梁，解雇了他的幕僚长，并在未事先通知的情况下和C-SPAN（公共事务卫星有线电视网，实况转播美国国会现场等——编注）进行了电话连线。 In other words, this is all unfolding exactly as expected. The news has been bad, and Mr. Trump knows it. Cue the mayhem. 换言之，一切都和预料的一样。坏消息接踵而至，特朗普对此心知肚明。于是，混乱开场了。 “We were having a very bad press day,” Mr. Trump told reporters on Monday about why he suggested on social media that the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship should turn the briefing room into his personal octagon. “I said, you know, I think I’m going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary.” “我们度过了新闻报道非常糟糕的一天，”关于为什么他在社交媒体上建议UFC首席执行官应把简报室变成其个人的八角笼，特朗普周一向记者解释道。“我说，你知道的，我想我要让达纳·怀特来当我的新一任新闻秘书。” Mr. Trump loves to change an unflattering headline by whipping out a diversion. But his usual tricks seem particularly discordant in the face of the urgent challenges facing the White House. There is an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, wars in Ukraine and Iran that the president promised to resolve months or years ago, and an incoming Congress whose Democratic majority is hungry to hold administration officials to account. 特朗普喜欢通过突然抛出一个转移注意力的噱头来扭转不利的新闻。但面对白宫眼下面临的紧迫挑战，他惯用的伎俩似乎显得尤为不合时宜。目前有人正推动弹劾国防部长皮特·海格塞斯；总统数月乃至数年前承诺解决的伊朗和乌克兰战争仍在继续；此外，即将上任的民主党多数国会正急于追究政府官员的责任。 But so far, Mr. Trump’s answer to the pressure has been to take an unserious approach to some of the most serious topics. In recent days, he has left the country guessing what he may do, what he may say, or even when he may show up in public. 但到目前为止，特朗普应对压力的对策是对一些最严肃的话题采取并不严肃的态度。最近几天，他让整个国家都在猜测他可能会做什么、说什么，甚至猜测他什么时候会在公开场合露面。 His advisers say the president thrives on chaos. The problem is that the public may not. 他的顾问们表示，总统在混乱中如鱼得水。问题在于，公众可能并非如此。 “We always talk about Donald Trump as the executive producer in chief,” said Doug Heye, a Republican strategist. “TV shows sort of run out of steam before they get to season six. That’s a big part of where voters are. They’re just exhausted.” “我们总是把唐纳德·特朗普称作‘首席执行制片人’，”共和党战略家道格·海伊说。“电视节目往往在播到第六季前热度就不行了。很大程度上，这也正是选民当下的状态。他们只是筋疲力尽了。” This extends to Mr. Trump repeating his baseless claims about election fraud. “It’s just not a credible argument, to the point that nobody’s paying attention,” Mr. Heye added. 这种疲态也体现在人们对特朗普重复其关于选举欺诈的无端指控上。“这根本不是一个可信的论点，以至于已经没人关注了，”海伊补充道。 Indeed, after the president on Monday revived claims that the midterm vote had been manipulated, the conservative commentator Megyn Kelly had a two-word retort: “Just stop.” 事实上，在总统周一重新提起中期选举投票被操纵的指控后，保守派评论员梅根·凯只回了寥寥几字：“得了吧。” Beni Rae Harmony, a White House spokeswoman, defended the president’s focus and productivity. 白宫发言人贝尼·雷·哈莫尼为总统的专注度及工作效率进行了辩护。 “President Trump never stops working, and his momentum has only increased in the past week,” she said in a statement, adding that he had held seven policy meetings, met with the Qatari prime minister and signed several bills into law, including one that designated a museum in Missouri as a national historic landmark and one that changes the bankruptcy threshold for small businesses. “特朗普总统从未停止工作，在过去的一周里他的动力只增不减，”她在一份声明中表示，并补充说总统举行了七次政策会议，会见了卡塔尔首相，并将数项法案签发为法律，其中包括一项将密苏里州的一家博物馆指定为国家历史地标的法案，以及一项修改小企业破产门槛的法案。 One adviser, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe the environment in the White House, called this moment a “natural transition phase.” 一位要求匿名以描述白宫当前氛围的顾问，将这一时刻称为“自然的过渡阶段”。 This is a sanguine descriptor, given the abrupt departure of Susie Wiles, the chief of staff Mr. Trump replaced with Stephen Miller, a hard-line loyalist who has driven many of the policies voters rejected last week. A Republican fratricide has also been playing out on social media, where current and former Trump officials have spent the past several days blaming each other for the midterm failures, trading accusations of corruption and grift, and threatening lawsuits. 这是一个颇为乐观的描述，因为前幕僚长苏西·怀尔斯刚遭遇突然解职，而特朗普用斯蒂芬·米勒接替了她。米勒是一名强硬的忠诚派，曾推动了许多在上周遭选民抵制的政策。同时，一场共和党人的内斗也正在社交媒体上上演，在过去的几天里，现任和前任特朗普政府官员一直在为中期选举的失利互相指责，相互指控对方腐败和敛财，并威胁要提起诉讼。 It is the Republican version of the scene in the 2004 movie “Mean Girls,” in which the main antagonist makes public a book full of private insults, unleashing bedlam inside a high school. 这就像是 2004 年电影《贱女孩》(Mean Girls)中某个场景的共和党翻版：在那场戏中，大反派公开了一本写满私人侮辱言辞的日记本，在一所高中里引发了轩然大波。 After spending a weekend at Mar-a-Lago golfing and delivering impromptu remarks at a conservative gathering on his property, Mr. Trump sought to distract from the bad headlines and the mounting congressional support for the impeachment of his defense secretary. On Monday, he startled reporters with an appearance in the White House briefing room. 在马阿拉歌度过了一个高尔夫周末、在那里的一场保守派集会上发表即兴讲话后，特朗普试图转移人们对负面新闻以及国会支持弹劾其国防部长的呼声不断高涨的关注。周一，他出人意料地现身白宫简报室，令记者们感到惊讶。 Mr. Trump riffed about his gambit of offering the press secretary gig to Mr. White, who accompanied him to greet reporters, and then began fielding questions of national and international import. 特朗普随口拿他提议怀特担任新闻秘书的把戏开起了玩笑——当时怀特也随他一起前来和记者们打招呼，随后便开始回答一些重要的国内外问题。 Asked about the admission by Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, of an affair with a Chinese businesswoman U.S. officials concluded was an intelligence operative for Beijing, the president seemed unconcerned, saying he bought Mr. Huang’s explanation. 当被问及英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与一名中国女商人有染（美国官员断定该女子为北京的情报人员）一事时，总统似乎毫不关心，表示自己相信黄仁勋的解释。 “He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Mr. Trump said. “他说，‘我完全不知道她是间谍，’而我真的相信他，”特朗普说。 The president also discussed the death toll in the Russia-Ukraine war, framing his assessment of the carnage in terms he understood: crowd sizes. 总统还讨论了俄乌战争的死亡人数，用他最熟悉的词汇——观众群规模，来表达他对这场惨烈杀戮的评估。 “I just think that Ukraine and Russia are tired of fighting. They’re tired of seeing dead young soldiers, mostly soldiers. Most of the people are soldiers. Think of it. They’re losing 25,000 — Dana, can you imagine 25,000? That’s like a stadium, Madison Square Garden. You have your fights, 25,000. That’s what it holds, and they’re losing that every single month, dead, young beautiful people, and it’s — it’s got to stop.” “我只是认为乌克兰和俄罗斯都厌倦了战斗。他们厌倦了看到年轻士兵死去，主要是士兵。死的大多是士兵。想想看。他们损失了2.5万人——达纳，你能想象2.5万人吗？那就是个体育场了，像麦迪逊广场花园那样的。你办比赛，2.5万人。那就是它的容量，而他们每个月都在失去这么多人，死去的、年轻漂亮的人，而这——这必须停止。” The fun and games continued later on Monday when Mr. Trump called into the premiere of a C-SPAN show, apparently without notice. A woman could be heard giggling in the background as the president’s call connected. 这场玩笑和游戏在周一晚些时候还在继续。当时特朗普似乎在没有预先通知的情况下，拨通了C-SPAN一档首播节目的热线。当总统的电话接通时，可以听到背景中有一名女子在咯咯地笑。 For eight minutes, Mimi Geerges, the host of the program, tried to press Mr. Trump about news he had made in several other interviews since the midterm elections. What about that immigration deal he had suggested he could strike with Democrats? What about amnesty for some migrant workers, as he had suggested on “60 Minutes” over the weekend? 在八分钟的通话里，该节目主持人米米·格尔吉斯试图就特朗普自中期选举以来在其他几次采访中引出的话题追问他。他之前暗示可能与民主党人达成的那项移民协议进展如何了？他周末在《60分钟》节目中暗示的、给予部分移民人员的特赦又是怎么回事？ His responses were not clarifying. 他的回答并未起到任何澄清作用。 “Frankly, a big problem we had is the mental institutions being dumped into our country. Some very dangerous people were released into our country, to put it mildly. So we have not put the same, uh, pressure, obviously, and, you know, the, uh, we call them the worst of the worst,” Mr. Trump said, by way of an answer. “We haven’t put the same pressure on waitresses and, and on farm workers, et cetera. Not even close.” “坦率地说，我们面临的一个大问题是精神病院里的人被倾倒进我们的国家。说得委婉点，一些极其危险的人被释放到了我们的国家。所以，我们显然没有施加同样的，呃，压力，而且，你知道的，那个，呃，我们称他们为最坏中的最坏，”特朗普如此回答道。“我们没有对女服务员和农场工人等人群施加同等的压力。差得远了。” Natural transition phase or not, many Republicans are worried that the White House will not be able to deliver on the request made by voters last week, which was to get serious about addressing economic concerns, an unchecked war and accusations of rampant corruption among those in Mr. Trump’s orbit. 无论这是否属于“自然的过渡阶段”，许多共和党人都担心，白宫将无法满足选民上周提出的要求——即认真应对经济担忧、一场不受控制的战争，以及针对特朗普核心圈子里猖獗腐败的指控。 The best-case scenario, said the G.O.P. strategist Whit Ayres, would be if the administration followed through “on Trump’s initial instinct to do something with the Democrats who are going to be running the place shortly.” 共和党策略师惠特·艾尔斯表示，最好的情况将是，政府能够顺应“特朗普最初的直觉，与不久后即将接管这里的民主党人一起合作做些什么”。 But, he added, “I think the chances of that happening are somewhere between slim and none.” 但是，他补充道，“我认为这种情况发生的几率微乎其微。” Katie Rogers是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。

That’s a big part of where voters are. They’re just exhausted.” “我们总是把唐纳德·特朗普称作‘首席执行制片人’，”共和党战略家道格·海伊说。“电视节目往往在播到第六季前热度就不行了。很大程度上，这也正是选民当下的状态。他们只是筋疲力尽了。” This extends to Mr. Trump repeating his baseless claims about election fraud. “It’s just not a credible argument, to the point that nobody’s paying attention,” Mr. Heye added. 这种疲态也体现在人们对特朗普重复其关于选举欺诈的无端指控上。“这根本不是一个可信的论点，以至于已经没人关注了，”海伊补充道。 Indeed, after the president on Monday revived claims that the midterm vote had been manipulated, the conservative commentator Megyn Kelly had a two-word retort: “Just stop.” 事实上，在总统周一 重新提起 中期选举投票被操纵的指控后，保守派评论员梅根·凯只回了寥寥几字：“得了吧。” Beni Rae Harmony, a White House spokeswoman, defended the president’s focus and productivity. 白宫发言人贝尼·雷·哈莫尼为总统的专注度及工作效率进行了辩护。 “President Trump never stops working, and his momentum has only increased in the past week,” she said in a statement, adding that he had held seven policy meetings, met with the Qatari prime minister and signed several bills into law, including one that designated a museum in Missouri as a national historic landmark and one that changes the bankruptcy threshold for small businesses. “特朗普总统从未停止工作，在过去的一周里他的动力只增不减，”她在一份声明中表示，并补充说总统举行了七次政策会议，会见了卡塔尔首相，并 将数项法案 签发为法律，其中包括一项将密苏里州的一家博物馆指定为国家历史地标的法案，以及一项修改小企业破产门槛的法案。 One adviser, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe the environment in the White House, called this moment a “natural transition phase.” 一位要求匿名以描述白宫当前氛围的顾问，将这一时刻称为“自然的过渡阶段”。 This is a sanguine descriptor, given the abrupt departure of Susie Wiles, the chief of staff Mr. Trump replaced with Stephen Miller, a hard-line loyalist who has driven many of the policies voters rejected last week. A Republican fratricide has also been playing out on social media, where current and former Trump officials have spent the past several days blaming each other for the midterm failures, trading accusations of corruption and grift, and threatening lawsuits. 这是一个颇为乐观的描述，因为前幕僚长苏西·怀尔斯刚遭遇突然解职，而特朗普用斯蒂芬·米勒接替了她。米勒是一名强硬的忠诚派，曾 推动了许多 在上周遭选民抵制的政策。同时，一场共和党人的内斗也正在社交媒体上上演，在过去的几天里，现任和前任特朗普政府官员一直在为中期选举的失利互相指责，相互 指控 对方腐败和敛财，并威胁要提起诉讼。 It is the Republican version of the scene in the 2004 movie “Mean Girls,” in which the main antagonist makes public a book full of private insults, unleashing bedlam inside a high school. 这就像是 2004 年电影《贱女孩》(Mean Girls)中某个场景的共和党翻版：在那场戏中，大反派公开了一本写满私人侮辱言辞的日记本，在一所高中里引发了轩然大波。 After spending a weekend at Mar-a-Lago golfing and delivering impromptu remarks at a conservative gathering on his property, Mr. Trump sought to distract from the bad headlines and the mounting congressional support for the impeachment of his defense secretary. On Monday, he startled reporters with an appearance in the White House briefing room. 在马阿拉歌度过了一个高尔夫周末、在那里的一场保守派集会上发表即兴讲话后，特朗普试图转移人们对负面新闻以及国会支持弹劾其国防部长的呼声不断高涨的关注。周一，他出人意料地现身白宫简报室，令记者们感到惊讶。 Mr. Trump riffed about his gambit of offering the press secretary gig to Mr. White, who accompanied him to greet reporters, and then began fielding questions of national and international import. 特朗普随口拿他提议怀特担任新闻秘书的把戏开起了玩笑——当时怀特也随他一起前来和记者们打招呼，随后便开始回答一些重要的国内外问题。 Asked about the admission by Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, of an affair with a Chinese businesswoman U.S. officials concluded was an intelligence operative for Beijing, the president seemed unconcerned, saying he bought Mr. Huang’s explanation. 当被问及英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与一名 中国女商人 有染（美国官员断定该女子为北京的情报人员）一事时，总统似乎毫不关心，表示自己相信黄仁勋的解释。 “He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Mr. Trump said. “他说，‘我完全不知道她是间谍，’而我真的相信他，”特朗普说。 The president also discussed the death toll in the Russia-Ukraine war, framing his assessment of the carnage in terms he understood: crowd sizes. 总统还讨论了俄乌战争的死亡人数，用他最熟悉的词汇——观众群规模，来表达他对这场惨烈杀戮的评估。 “I just think that Ukraine and Russia are tired of fighting. They’re tired of seeing dead young soldiers, mostly soldiers. Most of the people are soldiers. Think of it. They’re losing 25,000 — Dana, can you imagine 25,000? That’s like a stadium, Madison Square Garden. You have your fights, 25,000. That’s what it holds, and they’re losing that every single month, dead, young beautiful people, and it’s — it’s got to stop.” “我只是认为乌克兰和俄罗斯都厌倦了战斗。他们厌倦了看到年轻士兵死去，主要是士兵。死的大多是士兵。想想看。他们损失了2.5万人——达纳，你能想象2.5万人吗？那就是个体育场了，像麦迪逊广场花园那样的。你办比赛，2.5万人。那就是它的容量，而他们每个月都在失去这么多人，死去的、年轻漂亮的人，而这——这必须停止。” The fun and games continued later on Monday when Mr. Trump called into the premiere of a C-SPAN show, apparently without notice. A woman could be heard giggling in the background as the president’s call connected. 这场玩笑和游戏在周一晚些时候还在继续。当时特朗普似乎在没有预先通知的情况下，拨通了C-SPAN一档首播节目的热线。当总统的电话接通时，可以听到背景中有一名女子在咯咯地笑。 For eight minutes, Mimi Geerges, the host of the program, tried to press Mr. Trump about news he had made in several other interviews since the midterm elections. What about that immigration deal he had suggested he could strike with Democrats? What about amnesty for some migrant workers, as he had suggested on “60 Minutes” over the weekend? 在八分钟的通话里，该节目主持人米米·格尔吉斯试图就特朗普自中期选举以来在其他几次采访中引出的话题追问他。他之前暗示可能与民主党人达成的那项移民协议进展如何了？他周末在《60分钟》节目中暗示的、给予部分移民人员的特赦又是怎么回事？ His responses were not clarifying. 他的回答并未起到任何澄清作用。 “Frankly, a big problem we had is the mental institutions being dumped into our country. Some very dangerous people were released into our country, to put it mildly. So we have not put the same, uh, pressure, obviously, and, you know, the, uh, we call them the worst of the worst,” Mr. Trump said, by way of an answer. “We haven’t put the same pressure on waitresses and, and on farm workers, et cetera. Not even close.” “坦率地说，我们面临的一个大问题是精神病院里的人被倾倒进我们的国家。说得委婉点，一些极其危险的人被释放到了我们的国家。所以，我们显然没有施加同样的，呃，压力，而且，你知道的，那个，呃，我们称他们为最坏中的最坏，”特朗普如此回答道。“我们没有对女服务员和农场工人等人群施加同等的压力。差得远了。” Natural transition phase or not, many Republicans are worried that the White House will not be able to deliver on the request made by voters last week, which was to get serious about addressing economic concerns, an unchecked war and accusations of rampant corruption among those in Mr. Trump’s orbit. 无论这是否属于“自然的过渡阶段”，许多共和党人都担心，白宫将无法满足选民上周提出的要求——即认真应对经济担忧、一场不受控制的战争，以及针对特朗普核心圈子里猖獗腐败的指控。 The best-case scenario, said the G.O.P. strategist Whit Ayres, would be if the administration followed through “on Trump’s initial instinct to do something with the Democrats who are going to be running the place shortly.” 共和党策略师惠特·艾尔斯表示，最好的情况将是，政府能够顺应“特朗普最初的直觉，与不久后即将接管这里的民主党人一起合作做些什么”。 But, he added, “I think the chances of that happening are somewhere between slim and none.” 但是，他补充道，“我认为这种情况发生的几率微乎其微。” Katie Rogers 是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 富人越来越富，也越来越坏
description: MOLLY JONG-FAST2026年11月11日 Ryan Evans The weekend before Election Day, I opened up Instagram and saw an image so jarring that I first thought it was A.I.-generated. Martha Stewart had dressed up as a poor person for Halloween. She wore ripped jeans and a weather-beaten flannel, and had what looked like dirt smeared across her face. She held a sign that said “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” and turned her lips down into a mocking frown. The caption directed her audience toward her branded candle collection. 选举日前的那个周末，我打开Instagram，看到一张令人震惊的照片，第一反应是这一定是人工智能生成的。玛莎·斯图尔特在万圣节把自己打扮成了一个穷人。她穿着破洞牛仔裤和一件显得十分陈旧的法兰绒衬衫，脸上好像抹了泥。她举着一块牌子，上面写着“我饿了，帮帮我！！”，嘴角故意向下撇，做出嘲弄的苦相。配文则引导粉丝去购买她自己品牌的蜡烛系列。 Ms. Stewart’s Halloween costume is the sort of thing we’ve been seeing from rich people since President Trump’s second election. Many regular voters went for Mr. Trump in 2024 because of the high cost of groceries. But rich people felt empowered by his second victory, as if the public elected them, too. 自特朗普总统第二次当选以来，我们经常看到富人做出斯图尔特这种事。2024年，许多普通选民因为食品价格高企而把票投给特朗普。但他的再次胜选却让富人觉得自己也获得了某种授权，仿佛选民把他们也选上了台。 And so it’s been two years of rich people going full Roman emperor — unleashed, unapologetic and, often, punching down. 于是，过去两年里，富人们越来越像罗马皇帝，肆无忌惮、毫无歉意，而且常常恃强凌弱。 For much of my life, I’ve spent a lot of time with wealthy people in places like New York City and Los Angeles. My family, literary types, were not Wall Street banker rich or industrialist rich, like some of my friends and neighbors. I miss that brand of rich person. They had some vague WASP-y reticence about showing off. Some of them drove old Volvos. Few of them flew first class, let alone private. Besides, the New York of the 1980s was a place where showoffs tended to get mugged. If someone was mind-bendingly wealthy, that person didn’t necessarily want you to know it. 我人生中的大部分时间都经常在纽约和洛杉矶等地与富人打交道。我的家人都是文学圈人士，不像我的一些朋友和邻居那样，是华尔街银行家或实业家级别的富豪。我怀念从前那种富人。他们多少还保留着一点盎格鲁-撒克逊白人新教徒式的低调，不愿炫耀财富。有些人开着旧沃尔沃。很少有人坐头等舱，更不用说私人飞机了。况且，1980年代的纽约是个爱炫富的人容易遭抢劫的地方。即使一个人富得令人难以想象，也未必愿意让别人知道。 Today’s rich people are richer than ever, and that seems to have made them worse than ever. More shameless. More out of touch. Less empathetic. Thinner-skinned. And, for some mysterious reason, angrier. They’re people who consider equality for others oppression for themselves. 如今的富人比以往任何时候都更富有，而这似乎也让他们变得比以往任何时候都更糟糕。他们更加无耻，更加脱离现实，更缺乏同理心，更受不得批评。而且，不知为什么，他们还更加愤怒。在这些人看来，别人获得平等，就意味着自己受到了压迫。 Sometimes they’re nouveau riche ridiculous — Jeff Bezos throwing a foam party on his half-billion-dollar yacht and then occupying Venice for his star-studded wedding. Or they’re destabilizing — Elon Musk dancing with a chain saw and hacking away at the federal government, a move that threw hundreds of thousands of people out of the federal work force and cost taxpayers an estimated $135 billion last year. Too often, they’ve been flashing their wealth before our eyes. Mr. Trump’s billionaire buddies kissed up and paid up — pass the hat for the inauguration, boys! — and ended up with tax benefits. (See: “bonus depreciation,” which allows executives to write off depreciating assets and has led to a buying spree in both private planes and racehorses.) 有时，他们像暴发户一样荒唐可笑——杰夫·贝索斯在价值5亿美元的游艇上举办泡沫派对，又为了那场众星云集的婚礼，把威尼斯变成了自己的私人会场。有时，他们则会造成严重破坏——埃隆·马斯克挥舞着电锯跳舞，对联邦政府大砍大削，让数十万人丢了联邦政府的饭碗，据估计去年还让纳税人付出了1350亿美元的代价。他们也太频繁地在我们眼前炫耀财富。特朗普的亿万富豪朋友们一边阿谀奉承，一边慷慨解囊——来吧，哥儿几个，为就职典礼凑钱！——最终换来了税收优惠。（比如“额外折旧扣除”，允许企业高管对会贬值的资产进行税务抵扣，并引发了私人飞机和赛马的购买热潮。） It’s well documented that extreme wealth melts one’s brain. As Helen Riess and Liz Neporent write in “The Empathy Effect”: “Scientific studies have shown there is an inverse relationship between power and empathy. This distance often insulates the rich and powerful from the suffering of the everyday person.” The richer you are, the more insular your life becomes, and the more out of touch you become. Money becomes a way of measuring yourself against other rich people. It’s not about worrying about your rent, filling up your gas tank or affording ground beef at the grocery store. Get rich enough, and your doctor probably doesn’t even take health insurance — and you don’t need him to. 大量研究已经证明，巨额财富会把人的脑子烧坏。海伦·里斯和莉兹·内波伦特在《同理心效应》一书中写道：“科学研究表明，权力与同理心之间存在反比关系。这种距离往往使富人和权贵与普通人的苦难隔绝开来。”一个人越富有，生活圈子就越封闭，也就越脱离现实。金钱成了他们与其他富人比较的标尺。他们不必为房租、汽车加油或在超市买不买得起碎牛肉而发愁。只要足够有钱，你的医生很可能连医疗保险都不接受——而你也根本不需要他接受。 The wealthiest Americans’ X feeds must be puzzlingly filled with self-pity or the belief that somehow they are the ones being discriminated against in the world. Sergey Brin personally spent $100 million to help defeat the California wealth tax. And never mind all the squawking among the 17,000 New Yorkers who were asked by the Mamdani administration to prove that their $5-million-plus homes were not pieds-à-terre, and therefore subject to an extra tax. 美国最富有的那些人，X上的信息流里想必充斥着令人费解的自怜情绪，以及自己不知怎么成了受歧视者的论调。谢尔盖·布林个人花费了1亿美元，出资助力否决加州财富税。还有纽约那1.7万名富人的抱怨也不必说了。马姆达尼政府要求他们证明自己价值超过500万美元的住房不是偶尔落脚的第二居所，否则就要缴纳额外税款，他们为此叫苦连天。 Once upon a time, the wealthiest Americans knew they had it good and that they owed something to the rest of us. They followed in the spirit of Andrew Carnegie’s “The Gospel of Wealth,” in which he argued that the rich have a moral duty to help better the world, for everyone. They funded libraries, museums, medical research, disease eradication projects and even entire universities. Maybe this was out of moral or even religious conviction. Maybe it was out of a desire to see their names on buildings. Or maybe it was out of fear, after decades of strikes and social movements and, in other countries, revolutions. 曾几何时，美国最富有的人知道自己生活优渥，也明白自己对社会其他成员负有某种责任。他们奉行安德鲁·卡内基在《财富福音》中倡导的精神：富人有道德义务帮助建设一个对所有人都更美好的世界。他们出资兴建图书馆、博物馆，资助医学研究、疾病根除项目，甚至创办整所大学。也许他们这样做出于道德或宗教信念，也许只是想让自己的名字出现在建筑物上。又或许，在经历了数十年的罢工和社会运动，以及其他国家爆发的革命之后，他们心存恐惧。 Those lessons have been mostly forgotten. The wealthiest Americans don’t seem to care that much about giving back. When billionaires do give, it’s often to causes that appear to come with perks, like Mr. Trump’s inaugural fund or his ridiculous ballroom. 这些教训如今大多被遗忘了。美国最富有的人似乎不再那么关心回馈社会。即使亿万富豪愿意捐款，也往往是捐给那些看起来能为自己带来好处的项目，比如特朗普的就职基金，或者他那座荒唐的宴会厅。 It looks as if, finally, regular Americans have had enough. On the whole, voters rebuked Mr. Trump’s by-billionaires-for-billionaires government in stunning fashion in last week’s midterms. They won’t be bought or bribed away from reality, and they’ll turn out in droves before they’ll let Elon Musk buy their elections. When the president tried to dangle a $5,000 check in front of voters, they just said no. 如今看来，普通美国人终于受够了。总体而言，在上周的中期选举中，选民以惊人的方式教训了特朗普那个由亿万富翁组成、为亿万富翁服务的政府。他们不会被金钱收买，也不会被利益诱惑而无视现实。他们宁愿大批走进投票站，也不愿让埃隆·马斯克凭借财力左右选举。当总统试图用一张5000美元的支票诱惑选民时，他们干脆地说了不。 Affordability became a midterm buzzword because it’s a real crisis. During Mr. Trump’s second term, prices for staples like gas, diesel, beef and coffee have skyrocketed. Medicare and Obamacare cuts are throwing millions off health insurance. The One Big Beautiful Bill stripped millions of people of the SNAP benefits they need to feed their families. While Mr. Trump obsesses about a plethora of construction projects including a ballroom, normal people are poorer and angrier than they were when they elected him. 生活负担成为中期选举的热门词汇，是因为这确实是一场危机。特朗普第二任期内，汽油、柴油、牛肉和咖啡等生活必需品价格飞涨。联邦医疗保险和奥巴马医改项目遭到削减，导致数百万人失去医疗保险。《大而美法案》使数百万人失去了养家糊口所依赖的补充营养援助计划(SNAP）福利。特朗普却沉迷于包括宴会厅在内的一大堆建筑工程。普通人的生活比当初选他上台时更加拮据，也更加愤怒。 Cue Martha Stewart: “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” 这时轮到玛莎·斯图尔特登场了：“我饿了，帮帮我！！” What was she expecting people to do, write “yaaaas Hobo Queen!” in the comments? 她难道指望人们在评论区写下“哇哦，流浪女王万岁！”吗？ Ms. Stewart quickly took down her Instagram post and, after public outcry, apologized, multiple times. Then she started blaming someone else for her Halloween misstep. She said the “Today” show anchor Craig Melvin spilled chocolate on her sweater and that she dressed up that way because she had only 10 minutes to get ready. Shockingly, nobody’s really buying that excuse. 斯图尔特很快删除了那条Instagram帖文，并在公众强烈抗议后多次道歉。随后，她又开始把万圣节装扮失当的责任推给别人。她说，《今日》节目主持人克雷格·梅尔文把巧克力弄到了她的毛衣上，而她只有10分钟时间换装，所以才打扮成那个样子。不出所料，几乎没人相信这个借口。 Much like Mr. Trump and his billionaire buddies, she may have squandered her gilded age. 和特朗普及他的亿万富豪朋友们一样，她或许也已经挥霍掉了属于自己的镀金时代。 最受欢迎 接近黄仁勋的女间谍由中国国安部招募 为什么泰国医生“害怕”肯德基 中国前10个月贸易顺差突破1万亿美元 黄仁勋承认出轨，英伟达调查其与疑似中国间谍的关系 美、中、俄三国首脑在深圳会晤？习近平的雄心与顾虑 北京否认与黄仁勋有亲密关系的女性为中国间谍 英伟达先进芯片流向中国“空壳”公司 黄仁勋对特朗普称自己不知婚外情对象疑似中国间谍 美国商务部就芯片展开的调查在英伟达介入后中止 黄仁勋对英伟达的全面控制是否意味着他难以被惩罚 国际 中国 商业与经济 镜头 科技 科学 健康 教育 文化 风尚 旅游 房地产 观点与评论 国际 亚太 南亚 美国 美洲 欧洲 中东 非洲 中国 时政 经济 社会 中外关系 港澳台 商业与经济 全球经济 中国经济 交易录 文化 阅读 艺术 电影与电视 体育 风尚 时尚 美食与美酒 生活方式 观点与评论 专栏作者 观点 漫画 更多 镜头 科技 科技公司 科技与你 科学 健康 教育 旅游 房地产 免费下载 纽约时报中文网 iOS 和 Android App 点击下载iOS App 点击下载Android App© 2026 The New York Times Company.
content: MOLLY JONG-FAST 2026年11月11日 Ryan Evans The weekend before Election Day, I opened up Instagram and saw an image so jarring that I first thought it was A.I.-generated. Martha Stewart had dressed up as a poor person for Halloween. She wore ripped jeans and a weather-beaten flannel, and had what looked like dirt smeared across her face. She held a sign that said “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” and turned her lips down into a mocking frown. The caption directed her audience toward her branded candle collection. 选举日前的那个周末，我打开Instagram，看到一张令人震惊的照片，第一反应是这一定是人工智能生成的。玛莎·斯图尔特在万圣节把自己打扮成了一个穷人。她穿着破洞牛仔裤和一件显得十分陈旧的法兰绒衬衫，脸上好像抹了泥。她举着一块牌子，上面写着“我饿了，帮帮我！！”，嘴角故意向下撇，做出嘲弄的苦相。配文则引导粉丝去购买她自己品牌的蜡烛系列。 Ms. Stewart’s Halloween costume is the sort of thing we’ve been seeing from rich people since President Trump’s second election. Many regular voters went for Mr. Trump in 2024 because of the high cost of groceries. But rich people felt empowered by his second victory, as if the public elected them, too. 自特朗普总统第二次当选以来，我们经常看到富人做出斯图尔特这种事。2024年，许多普通选民因为食品价格高企而把票投给特朗普。但他的再次胜选却让富人觉得自己也获得了某种授权，仿佛选民把他们也选上了台。 And so it’s been two years of rich people going full Roman emperor — unleashed, unapologetic and, often, punching down. 于是，过去两年里，富人们越来越像罗马皇帝，肆无忌惮、毫无歉意，而且常常恃强凌弱。 For much of my life, I’ve spent a lot of time with wealthy people in places like New York City and Los Angeles. My family, literary types, were not Wall Street banker rich or industrialist rich, like some of my friends and neighbors. I miss that brand of rich person. They had some vague WASP-y reticence about showing off. Some of them drove old Volvos. Few of them flew first class, let alone private. Besides, the New York of the 1980s was a place where showoffs tended to get mugged. If someone was mind-bendingly wealthy, that person didn’t necessarily want you to know it. 我人生中的大部分时间都经常在纽约和洛杉矶等地与富人打交道。我的家人都是文学圈人士，不像我的一些朋友和邻居那样，是华尔街银行家或实业家级别的富豪。我怀念从前那种富人。他们多少还保留着一点盎格鲁-撒克逊白人新教徒式的低调，不愿炫耀财富。有些人开着旧沃尔沃。很少有人坐头等舱，更不用说私人飞机了。况且，1980年代的纽约是个爱炫富的人容易遭抢劫的地方。即使一个人富得令人难以想象，也未必愿意让别人知道。 Today’s rich people are richer than ever, and that seems to have made them worse than ever. More shameless. More out of touch. Less empathetic. Thinner-skinned. And, for some mysterious reason, angrier. They’re people who consider equality for others oppression for themselves. 如今的富人比以往任何时候都更富有，而这似乎也让他们变得比以往任何时候都更糟糕。他们更加无耻，更加脱离现实，更缺乏同理心，更受不得批评。而且，不知为什么，他们还更加愤怒。在这些人看来，别人获得平等，就意味着自己受到了压迫。 Sometimes they’re nouveau riche ridiculous — Jeff Bezos throwing a foam party on his half-billion-dollar yacht and then occupying Venice for his star-studded wedding. Or they’re destabilizing — Elon Musk dancing with a chain saw and hacking away at the federal government, a move that threw hundreds of thousands of people out of the federal work force and cost taxpayers an estimated $135 billion last year. Too often, they’ve been flashing their wealth before our eyes. Mr. Trump’s billionaire buddies kissed up and paid up — pass the hat for the inauguration, boys! — and ended up with tax benefits. (See: “bonus depreciation,” which allows executives to write off depreciating assets and has led to a buying spree in both private planes and racehorses.) 有时，他们像暴发户一样荒唐可笑——杰夫·贝索斯在价值5亿美元的游艇上举办泡沫派对，又为了那场众星云集的婚礼，把威尼斯变成了自己的私人会场。有时，他们则会造成严重破坏——埃隆·马斯克挥舞着电锯跳舞，对联邦政府大砍大削，让数十万人丢了联邦政府的饭碗，据估计去年还让纳税人付出了 1350亿美元 的代价。他们也太频繁地在我们眼前炫耀财富。特朗普的亿万富豪朋友们一边阿谀奉承，一边慷慨解囊——来吧，哥儿几个，为就职典礼凑钱！——最终换来了税收优惠。（比如“ 额外折旧扣除 ”，允许企业高管对会贬值的资产进行税务抵扣，并引发了私人飞机和赛马的 购买热潮 。） It’s well documented that extreme wealth melts one’s brain. As Helen Riess and Liz Neporent write in “The Empathy Effect”: “Scientific studies have shown there is an inverse relationship between power and empathy. This distance often insulates the rich and powerful from the suffering of the everyday person.” The richer you are, the more insular your life becomes, and the more out of touch you become. Money becomes a way of measuring yourself against other rich people. It’s not about worrying about your rent, filling up your gas tank or affording ground beef at the grocery store. Get rich enough, and your doctor probably doesn’t even take health insurance — and you don’t need him to. 大量研究已经证明，巨额财富会把人的脑子烧坏。海伦·里斯和莉兹·内波伦特在《同理心效应》一书中写道：“科学研究表明，权力与同理心之间存在反比关系。这种距离往往使富人和权贵与普通人的苦难隔绝开来。”一个人越富有，生活圈子就越封闭，也就越脱离现实。金钱成了他们与其他富人比较的标尺。他们不必为房租、汽车加油或在超市买不买得起碎牛肉而发愁。只要足够有钱，你的医生很可能连医疗保险都不接受——而你也根本不需要他接受。 The wealthiest Americans’ X feeds must be puzzlingly filled with self-pity or the belief that somehow they are the ones being discriminated against in the world. Sergey Brin personally spent $100 million to help defeat the California wealth tax. And never mind all the squawking among the 17,000 New Yorkers who were asked by the Mamdani administration to prove that their $5-million-plus homes were not pieds-à-terre, and therefore subject to an extra tax. 美国最富有的那些人，X上的信息流里想必充斥着令人费解的自怜情绪，以及自己不知怎么成了受歧视者的论调。谢尔盖·布林个人花费了1亿美元，出资助力否决加州财富税。还有纽约那 1.7万名富人 的抱怨也不必说了。马姆达尼政府要求他们证明自己价值超过500万美元的住房不是偶尔落脚的第二居所，否则就要缴纳额外税款，他们为此叫苦连天。 Once upon a time, the wealthiest Americans knew they had it good and that they owed something to the rest of us. They followed in the spirit of Andrew Carnegie’s “The Gospel of Wealth,” in which he argued that the rich have a moral duty to help better the world, for everyone. They funded libraries, museums, medical research, disease eradication projects and even entire universities. Maybe this was out of moral or even religious conviction. Maybe it was out of a desire to see their names on buildings. Or maybe it was out of fear, after decades of strikes and social movements and, in other countries, revolutions. 曾几何时，美国最富有的人知道自己生活优渥，也明白自己对社会其他成员负有某种责任。他们奉行安德鲁·卡内基在《财富福音》中倡导的精神：富人有道德义务帮助建设一个对所有人都更美好的世界。他们出资兴建图书馆、博物馆，资助医学研究、疾病根除项目，甚至创办整所大学。也许他们这样做出于道德或宗教信念，也许只是想让自己的名字出现在建筑物上。又或许，在经历了数十年的罢工和社会运动，以及其他国家爆发的革命之后，他们心存恐惧。 Those lessons have been mostly forgotten. The wealthiest Americans don’t seem to care that much about giving back. When billionaires do give, it’s often to causes that appear to come with perks, like Mr. Trump’s inaugural fund or his ridiculous ballroom. 这些教训如今大多被遗忘了。美国最富有的人似乎不再那么关心回馈社会。即使亿万富豪愿意捐款，也往往是捐给那些看起来能为自己带来好处的项目，比如特朗普的就职基金，或者他那座荒唐的宴会厅。 It looks as if, finally, regular Americans have had enough. On the whole, voters rebuked Mr. Trump’s by-billionaires-for-billionaires government in stunning fashion in last week’s midterms. They won’t be bought or bribed away from reality, and they’ll turn out in droves before they’ll let Elon Musk buy their elections . When the president tried to dangle a $5,000 check in front of voters, they just said no. 如今看来，普通美国人终于受够了。总体而言，在上周的中期选举中，选民以惊人的方式教训了特朗普那个由亿万富翁组成、为亿万富翁服务的政府。他们不会被金钱收买，也不会被利益诱惑而无视现实。他们宁愿大批走进投票站，也 不愿让埃隆·马斯克凭借财力左右选举 。当总统试图用一张5000美元的支票诱惑选民时，他们干脆地说了不。 Affordability became a midterm buzzword because it’s a real crisis. During Mr. Trump’s second term, prices for staples like gas, diesel, beef and coffee have skyrocketed. Medicare and Obamacare cuts are throwing millions off health insurance. The One Big Beautiful Bill stripped millions of people of the SNAP benefits they need to feed their families. While Mr. Trump obsesses about a plethora of construction projects including a ballroom, normal people are poorer and angrier than they were when they elected him. 生活负担成为中期选举的热门词汇，是因为这确实是一场危机。特朗普第二任期内，汽油、柴油、牛肉和咖啡等生活必需品价格飞涨。联邦医疗保险和奥巴马医改项目遭到削减，导致 数百万人 失去医疗保险。《大而美法案》使数百万人失去了养家糊口所依赖的补充营养援助计划(SNAP）福利。特朗普却沉迷于包括宴会厅在内的一大堆建筑工程。普通人的生活比当初选他上台时更加拮据，也更加愤怒。 Cue Martha Stewart: “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” 这时轮到玛莎·斯图尔特登场了：“我饿了，帮帮我！！” What was she expecting people to do, write “yaaaas Hobo Queen!” in the comments? 她难道指望人们在评论区写下“哇哦，流浪女王万岁！”吗？ Ms. Stewart quickly took down her Instagram post and, after public outcry, apologized, multiple times. Then she started blaming someone else for her Halloween misstep. She said the “Today” show anchor Craig Melvin spilled chocolate on her sweater and that she dressed up that way because she had only 10 minutes to get ready. Shockingly, nobody’s really buying that excuse. 斯图尔特很快删除了那条Instagram帖文，并在公众强烈抗议后多次道歉。随后，她又开始把万圣节装扮失当的责任推给别人。她说，《今日》节目主持人克雷格·梅尔文 把巧克力弄到了她的毛衣上 ，而她只有10分钟时间换装，所以才打扮成那个样子。不出所料，几乎没人相信这个借口。 Much like Mr. Trump and his billionaire buddies, she may have squandered her gilded age. 和特朗普及他的亿万富豪朋友们一样，她或许也已经挥霍掉了属于自己的镀金时代。 最受欢迎 接近黄仁勋的女间谍由中国国安部招募 为什么泰国医生“害怕”肯德基 中国前10个月贸易顺差突破1万亿美元 黄仁勋承认出轨，英伟达调查其与疑似中国间谍的关系 美、中、俄三国首脑在深圳会晤？习近平的雄心与顾虑 北京否认与黄仁勋有亲密关系的女性为中国间谍 英伟达先进芯片流向中国“空壳”公司 黄仁勋对特朗普称自己不知婚外情对象疑似中国间谍 美国商务部就芯片展开的调查在英伟达介入后中止 黄仁勋对英伟达的全面控制是否意味着他难以被惩罚 国际 中国 商业与经济 镜头 科技 科学 健康 教育 文化 风尚 旅游 房地产 观点与评论 国际 亚太 南亚 美国 美洲 欧洲 中东 非洲 中国 时政 经济 社会 中外关系 港澳台 商业与经济 全球经济 中国经济 交易录 文化 阅读 艺术 电影与电视 体育 风尚 时尚 美食与美酒 生活方式 观点与评论 专栏作者 观点 漫画 更多 镜头 科技 科技公司 科技与你 科学 健康 教育 旅游 房地产 免费下载 纽约时报中文网 iOS 和 Android App 点击下载iOS App 点击下载Android App © 2026 The New York Times Company.

title: meta/astryx
description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready http://astryx.atmeta.com Astryx An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now: by people and the agents working alongside them. Currently in Beta · Built on React 19+ and StyleX Docs · Storybook · Sandbox · Contributing · Discord Overview Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day. It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling. What makes Astryx different: Open internals. Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. No styling lock-in. Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with className using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. Customize without wrapping. A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. Built for people and agents. The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference. Getting Started Astryx requires React 19 or later (react and react-dom are peer dependencies of @astryxdesign/core). Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies: # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli # yarn yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so astryx works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version: npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli Project install, global install, or both? astryx docs global/project-global-or-both compares them (both is recommended), and astryx docs global explains how global mode works. The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the @astryxdesign/core README for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN). For reliable CLI access, add a script to your package.json: "scripts": { "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs" } Then use it as npm run astryx -- component --list. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly. Packages Package Description README @astryxdesign/core Components, theme system, and utilities README @astryxdesign/cli CLI tooling: component docs, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods README @astryxdesign/build Build plugins for StyleX source builds README @astryxdesign/theme-* Seven ready-made, fully customizable themes (neutral, butter, chocolate, matcha, stone, gothic, y2k) README @astryxdesign/lab (experimental components) is used internally for Storybook and the sandbox and is not published to npm. @astryxdesign/vega (Vega/Vega-Lite chart wrapper) and @astryxdesign/charts (chart components) are published to npm only under the @canary dist-tag — there is no stable release yet. Principles These are the promises Astryx makes to the people building on it. Guidance over enforcement. Components give you capability rather than guardrails that fight you. Design opinions live in docs and examples — if you pass a value, the component renders it. Strong, documented conventions. Every component follows the same naming, prop, and composition rules, and every one is thoroughly documented — so once you've learned a few, the rest feel familiar, and both people and AI can predict how an unfamiliar component behaves. One system for humans and AI. The API, conventions, docs, and CLI are designed together so people and AI assistants build the same way. Every change that made Astryx easier for AI made it easier for people too. Earned by measurement. We test conventions rather than assert them, hold the results loosely, and revisit them when a new situation proves them wrong. Architecture Foundations The building blocks for visually cohesive and accessible interfaces: typography, color, layout, and accessibility. Components A library of 150+ reusable UI building blocks with full TypeScript support. Patterns Battle-tested design solutions for common interactions and workflows: table pages, detail page layouts, form wizards, navigation patterns, data entry flows. Project Structure Directory Purpose apps/ Example apps, the docsite, and Storybook packages/ Published packages: core, cli, build, themes internal/ Internal tooling: test utilities, eslint plugin, vibe tests Contributing We welcome contributions! See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full guide. Questions, or want a hand with a PR? Come find us in Discord. Our conventions and review rubrics live in the Contributing wiki — including API Conventions, Design Conventions, the Component Lifecycle, the Contributing Templates, and the Blog Review Rubric. Read the relevant rubric before opening a PR. Quick start for contributors: this repo uses Node 22+ on an active LTS line and pnpm 11. Install pnpm directly, or enable Corepack once so the pinned pnpm version installs automatically: corepack enable pnpm install If corepack is missing, install pnpm directly or install Corepack manually; see the troubleshooting notes in CONTRIBUTING.md. The Theme Showcase DOM tests use the root ui project for shared DOM and StyleX test setup. Run pnpm exec vitest run --project ui apps/docsite/src/__tests__/theme-showcase/ from the repository root. License MIT

Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies: # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli # yarn yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so astryx works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version: npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli Project install, global install, or both? astryx docs global/project-global-or-both compares them (both is recommended), and astryx docs global explains how global mode works. The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the @astryxdesign/core README for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN). For reliable CLI access, add a script to your package.json : "scripts": { "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs" } Then use it as npm run astryx -- component --list . This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly. Packages Package Description README @astryxdesign/core Components, theme system, and utilities README @astryxdesign/cli CLI tooling: component docs, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods README @astryxdesign/build Build plugins for StyleX source builds README @astryxdesign/theme-* Seven ready-made, fully customizable themes (neutral, butter, chocolate, matcha, stone, gothic, y2k) README @astryxdesign/lab (experimental components) is used internally for Storybook and the sandbox and is not published to npm. @astryxdesign/vega (Vega/Vega-Lite chart wrapper) and @astryxdesign/charts (chart components) are published to npm only under the @canary dist-tag — there is no stable release yet. Principles These are the promises Astryx makes to the people building on it. Guidance over enforcement. Components give you capability rather than guardrails that fight you. Design opinions live in docs and examples — if you pass a value, the component renders it. Strong, documented conventions. Every component follows the same naming, prop, and composition rules, and every one is thoroughly documented — so once you've learned a few, the rest feel familiar, and both people and AI can predict how an unfamiliar component behaves. One system for humans and AI. The API, conventions, docs, and CLI are designed together so people and AI assistants build the same way. Every change that made Astryx easier for AI made it easier for people too. Earned by measurement. We test conventions rather than assert them, hold the results loosely, and revisit them when a new situation proves them wrong. Architecture Foundations The building blocks for visually cohesive and accessible interfaces: typography, color, layout, and accessibility. Components A library of 150+ reusable UI building blocks with full TypeScript support. Patterns Battle-tested design solutions for common interactions and workflows: table pages, detail page layouts, form wizards, navigation patterns, data entry flows. Project Structure Directory Purpose apps/ Example apps, the docsite, and Storybook packages/ Published packages: core, cli, build, themes internal/ Internal tooling: test utilities, eslint plugin, vibe tests Contributing We welcome contributions! See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full guide. Questions, or want a hand with a PR? Come find us in Discord . Our conventions and review rubrics live in the Contributing wiki — including API Conventions , Design Conventions , the Component Lifecycle , the Contributing Templates , and the Blog Review Rubric . Read the relevant rubric before opening a PR. Quick start for contributors: this repo uses Node 22+ on an active LTS line and pnpm 11 . Install pnpm directly, or enable Corepack once so the pinned pnpm version installs automatically: corepack enable pnpm install If corepack is missing, install pnpm directly or install Corepack manually; see the troubleshooting notes in CONTRIBUTING.md . The Theme Showcase DOM tests use the root ui project for shared DOM and StyleX test setup. Run pnpm exec vitest run --project ui apps/docsite/src/__tests__/theme-showcase/ from the repository root. description: https://goo.gle/modern-web-guidance Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See CONTRIBUTING.md and GOVERNANCE.md for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community. Documentation · Eval Dashboard · Source Code · Report an Issue Quickstart npx modern-web-guidance@latest install This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See Alternative Installation Methods below. Try it out (without installing) # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap. Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: Modern Browser APIs: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. Performance & Accessibility: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. Responsible Fallbacks: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are designed to be token-efficient; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. Core Disciplines 🎨 User Experience Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color). 📐 CSS Layout Modern layout systems (container queries, subgrid, modern color spaces like oklch, text-wrap tuning, and line-height trimming). ⚡ Performance Speed optimizations (instant preloading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) diagnostics, and scheduling tasks via scheduler.yield). 📝 Forms & UI Native components (Anchor Positioning for tooltips, Popover API, dialogs, :user-invalid validation, and auto-sizing fields). ♿ Accessibility Important considerations (screen reader and keyboard operability, content navigation and discoverability). 🤖 Built-in AI Local client models (native translation, summarization, and language detection APIs). View an example: the navigation-drawer guide. Safe Adoption of Modern Features Progressive Enhancement & Nuanced Fallbacks: We distinguish between purely additive enhancements (like speculative preloading) which are safe to let older browsers silently ignore, and critical behaviors (like dialog controls or network beacons) where we write highly considered, low-overhead fallbacks. Responsible Fallbacks: We prioritize lightweight, case-specific custom fallbacks ( ". The tool matches the query to the best guide using an offline, zero-dependency embedding model and BM25 search engine (no network calls, no API keys). Guide Fetch: The agent retrieves the guide via modern-web-guidance retrieve , inserting targeted code patterns, gotchas, and fallbacks directly into its context window. Tip Note: We use npx to ensure the content doesn't go stale, but the CLI works offline, completely private and local. The npm package is self-contained, with no extra dependencies to ensure both low-latency and supply-chain security. Otherwise, consult your agent's documentation for updating plugins and skills. Evals to prove this works well We developed a robust eval harness to ensure that the content is empirically proven and continuously calibrated so AI agents write better code. We run automated evaluations using a closed-loop validation pipeline: [ Expert-authored guidance and demo ] │ ▼ [ Target generation ] ──> Tasks on real webapps, Golden solutions, Playwright graders │ ▼ [ Calibration loop ] ───> Runs Grader on Golden Solutions (Must Pass 100%) │ Runs Grader on Unmodified Base App (Must Fail 100%) ▼ [ E2E agent evals ] ────> Runs coding agents in guided vs. unguided modes Compares pass rates and accessibility w/ and w/o the skill Simulated Developer Tasks: We define realistic developer prompts against full base applications (daily-grind, devtools-times) that mimic real-world requests (e.g., "make my images load faster"). Prompts avoid naming APIs or features, testing whether the agent can naturally discover and apply the right guides. Static & Browser-Based Assertions: Playwright graders verify that each implementation requirement was followed—checking source patterns, computed styles, runtime DOM behaviors, and accessibility states. Self-Healing Calibration: Graders are calibrated against multi-agent (Claude/Codex/AGY) golden solutions (100% pass target) and an unmodified baseline application (0% pass target). E2E Testing: We measure coding agent performance on real tasks with and without guidance. The opportunity (100% - unguided pass rate) and uplift (guided - unguided pass rate) are key: if models already succeed without guidance, we prune redundant advice; where agents struggle, we refine guides to maximize uplift. content: https://goo.gle/modern-web-guidance Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See CONTRIBUTING.md and GOVERNANCE.md for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community. Documentation · Eval Dashboard · Source Code · Report an Issue Quickstart npx modern-web-guidance@latest install This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See Alternative Installation Methods below. Try it out (without installing) # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap. Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: Modern Browser APIs : Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. Performance & Accessibility : Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. Responsible Fallbacks : Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are designed to be token-efficient ; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. Core Disciplines 🎨 User Experience Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color ). 📐 CSS Layout Modern layout systems (container queries, subgrid , modern color spaces like oklch , text-wrap tuning, and line-height trimming). ⚡ Performance Speed optimizations (instant preloading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) diagnostics, and scheduling tasks via scheduler.yield ). 📝 Forms & UI Native components (Anchor Positioning for tooltips, Popover API, dialogs, :user-invalid validation, and auto-sizing fields). ♿ Accessibility Important considerations (screen reader and keyboard operability, content navigation and discoverability). 🤖 Built-in AI Local client models (native translation, summarization, and language detection APIs). View an example: the navigation-drawer guide . How It Works Activation : The coding agent activates the modern-web-guidance skill because of a relevant task. The agent is instructed to use the modern-web-guidance CLI for web platform queries. Local Semantic Search : The agent runs modern-web-guidance search "<query>" . The tool matches the query to the best guide using an offline, zero-dependency embedding model and BM25 search engine (no network calls, no API keys). Guide Fetch : The agent retrieves the guide via modern-web-guidance retrieve <guide-id> , inserting targeted code patterns, gotchas, and fallbacks directly into its context window. Tip Note: We use npx to ensure the content doesn't go stale, but the CLI works offline, completely private and local. The npm package is self-contained, with no extra dependencies to ensure both low-latency and supply-chain security. Alternative Installation Methods Vercel Skills CLI (aka npx skills ) npx skills add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance GitHub CLI gh skill install GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance Google Antigravity agy plugin install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance GitHub Copilot CLI /plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance /plugin install modern-web-guidance@googlechrome Claude Code Plugin /plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance /plugin install modern-web-guidance@googlechrome /plugin # Select GoogleChrome marketplace, press enter, enable AutoUpdate /reload-plugins Grok Build CLI grok plugin install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance --trust Kimi Code /plugins install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance OpenAI Codex codex plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance codex plugin add modern-web-guidance@googlechrome Updating If you installed the skill using npx modern-web-guidance@latest install , you can update with: npx modern-web-guidance@latest update . Otherwise, consult your agent's documentation for updating plugins and skills. Evals to prove this works well We developed a robust eval harness to ensure that the content is empirically proven and continuously calibrated so AI agents write better code. We run automated evaluations using a closed-loop validation pipeline: [ Expert-authored guidance and demo ] │ ▼ [ Target generation ] ──> Tasks on real webapps, Golden solutions, Playwright graders │ ▼ [ Calibration loop ] ───> Runs Grader on Golden Solutions (Must Pass 100%) │ Runs Grader on Unmodified Base App (Must Fail 100%) ▼ [ E2E agent evals ] ────> Runs coding agents in guided vs. unguided modes Compares pass rates and accessibility w/ and w/o the skill Simulated Developer Tasks : We define realistic developer prompts against full base applications ( daily-grind , devtools-times ) that mimic real-world requests (e.g., "make my images load faster"). Prompts avoid naming APIs or features, testing whether the agent can naturally discover and apply the right guides. Static & Browser-Based Assertions : Playwright graders verify that each implementation requirement was followed—checking source patterns, computed styles, runtime DOM behaviors, and accessibility states. Self-Healing Calibration : Graders are calibrated against multi-agent (Claude/Codex/AGY) golden solutions (100% pass target) and an unmodified baseline application (0% pass target). E2E Testing : We measure coding agent performance on real tasks with and without guidance. The opportunity (100% - unguided pass rate) and uplift (guided - unguided pass rate) are key: if models already succeed without guidance, we prune redundant advice; where agents struggle, we refine guides to maximize uplift. title: shadcn/improve
description: Use your most capable model to audit your codebase and write plans for cheaper models to execute. improve An agent skill that audits any codebase and writes implementation plans for other agents to execute. The idea: use your most capable model for the part where intelligence compounds — understanding the codebase, judging what's worth doing, writing the spec — and hand execution to cheaper models. The skill never implements anything itself. The plan is the product. you → /improve (expensive model, advises) plans/ → 001-fix-n-plus-one.md (self-contained specs) other agent → implements, tests, ships (cheap model, executes) Install npx skills add shadcn/improve Works in any agent that supports Agent Skills format. The plans it writes are plain markdown, so any agent (or human) can pick them up. Usage /improve full audit → prioritized findings → plans /improve quick cheap pass: hotspots, top findings only /improve deep exhaustive: every package, every category /improve security focused audit (also: perf, tests, bugs, ...) /improve branch audit only what the current branch changes /improve next feature suggestions — where to take the project /improve plan skip the audit, spec one thing /improve review-plan critique and tighten an existing plan /improve execute dispatch a cheaper executor, review its work /improve reconcile refresh the backlog: verify, unblock, retire /improve ... --issues also publish plans as GitHub issues How to use A typical first run, start to finish: Open your agent in the repo and run /improve (or /improve quick to keep it cheap). It maps the repo, audits it, and comes back with a findings table. Reply with the ones you want planned — "plan 1, 3 and 5". Plans land in plans/ — one file each, plus an index with the recommended order. Read them; they're meant to be reviewed. Hand a plan to any agent ("implement plans/001-*.md"), or let the skill run it: /improve execute 001. It dispatches a cheaper model in an isolated worktree, reviews the diff against the plan, and reports back with a verdict. Merging stays up to you. Next session, run /improve reconcile to clean up the backlog: verify what landed, refresh what drifted, unblock what got stuck. Before a PR, /improve branch does the same thing scoped to just what your branch changes. Example A run against shadcn/ui came back with findings like: | # | Finding | Category | Effort | Confidence | |---|------------------------------------------------|-----------|--------|------------| | 1 | shadow-config duplicated in search.ts/view.ts, | tech-debt | M | HIGH | | | copies already drifted (TODO at search.ts:31) | | | | | 2 | O(n²) icon migration (migrate-icons.ts:168) | perf | S | HIGH | …and rejected a few, with reasons recorded so they don't come back next run: - [SEC-01] https_proxy env var "SSRF": by-design — standard proxy convention, every CLI honors it. Not a finding. Picking #1 produced this plan — current code excerpted, exact steps, the repo's own test/lint commands as verification gates, and STOP conditions for when reality doesn't match. How it works Recon. Maps the repo: stack, conventions, and the exact build/test/lint commands — these become verification gates in every plan. It also ingests intent and design docs when present — ADRs (docs/adr/), PRDs, CONTEXT.md, DESIGN.md, PRODUCT.md — so decided tradeoffs aren't re-flagged as findings, direction suggestions stay grounded in stated product intent, and plans speak the repo's own vocabulary. Composes with any repo that already maintains these docs. Audit. Fans out parallel subagents across nine categories: correctness, security, performance, test coverage, tech debt, dependencies & migrations, DX, docs, and direction (feature suggestions — every one must cite evidence from the repo itself, no generic idea-slop). Every finding carries file:line evidence, impact, effort, and confidence. Vet. Subagents over-report, so the advisor re-reads every cited location itself before showing you anything — false positives get dropped, wrong attributions get corrected, rejections get recorded. Prioritize. Findings land in a table ordered by leverage (impact ÷ effort, weighted by confidence). You pick what becomes plans. Plan. One file per selected finding, written into plans/ with an index, priority order, and dependency graph. What makes the plans executable Plans are written for the weakest plausible executor — a model that has never seen the advisor session and may be much smaller. Three properties carry that: Self-contained. All context is inlined: exact file paths, current-state code excerpts, repo conventions with an exemplar file, verified commands. No "as discussed above." Verification gates. Every step ends with a command and its expected output. Done criteria are machine-checkable. The executor never has to judge whether it succeeded. Hard boundaries. Explicit out-of-scope lists, and STOP conditions — "if X, stop and report" — instead of letting a small model improvise when reality doesn't match the plan. Each plan also stamps the git commit it was written against, so executors run a mechanical drift check before touching anything. Closing the loop Plans aren't fire-and-forget: execute spawns a cheaper executor subagent in an isolated git worktree, hands it the plan, then reviews the result like a tech lead — re-runs every done criterion, checks scope compliance, reads the diff against intent. Verdict: approve (merging stays your call), send back for revision (max 2 rounds), or block and refine the plan. reconcile processes what happened since: verifies DONE plans still hold, investigates BLOCKED ones and rewrites around the obstacle, refreshes drifted plans, retires findings that got fixed independently. --issues publishes plans as GitHub issues — same self-contained body, so any agent or human can pick them up where work already lives. Hard rules Never modifies source code itself. The only writes go to plans/; executors edit only in disposable worktrees, and merging is always yours. Never runs commands that mutate your working tree — read, search, and read-only analysis only. Never reproduces secret values. Locations and credential types only, rotation always recommended. Asked to implement? It declines and points at the plan (or offers execute). License MIT © shadcn
